flags.title: Originated price arithmetic does not reconcile
flags.detail: 11 priced lines have a stated American price or probability that disagrees with the decimal price by more than tolerance. The decimal price is treated as the primary value and every published figure on this desk is recomputed from it.

flags.title: The requested High window is only 1.43 probability points wide
flags.detail: The brief asks for picks with a better-than-70% win chance priced between -250 and +10000. -250 is decimal 1.40, i.e. 71.43% implied. Any selection that is both above 70% and inside the window therefore has to sit between 70.00% and 71.43% — a band 1.43 points wide. Five picks per sport inside that band cannot be produced from real favourites: the genuine short-priced favourites (Perugia at 89%, Ireland at 80%, Kiel at 82%) are all shorter than -250 and are outside the window. This desk therefore publishes both: in-window picks as High, and stronger favourites outside the window clearly labelled as out-of-window rather than quietly squeezed into the band.

flags.title: Desk 496eaf02 labels 51 picks High; only 3 satisfy the brief's own conjunction
flags.detail: Its published market file contains 460 priced outcomes. Recomputing the stated rule (>70% AND -250..+10000) on its own numbers yields 3 qualifying lines, not 51. 33 lines sit above 70%, so most of the 51 are short-priced favourites that are outside the requested window. The desk's headline count and its own price data disagree; the row-level labels are not reproduced by this desk.

flags.title: One desk supplies almost the whole in-window pool, and its prices cluster at the threshold
flags.detail: 95 of 8a900c04's 472 priced lines sit between 0.700 and 0.720 (20.1%), against 1.7% for 496eaf02 and 1.4% for 65331685. That desk also supplies 84 of the 94 candidate lines that fall inside the brief's window. Of 1655 priced observations only 39 are seconded by another desk, and not one in-window line is priced twice. Dropping that desk entirely leaves 10 in-window candidates across 7 sports. The concentration, not the individual prices, is the finding: a price ladder tuned to land just above a published threshold cannot be read as independent agreement.

flags.title: No in-window line is corroborated, and the shared lines mostly disagree
flags.detail: All 94 in-window candidate lines are priced by a single desk: the brief's window is populated entirely by non-overlapping single-source estimates. Of the 39 lines that two desks do price, 1 agrees within 0.02 decimal and 38 differ by more than that. Every pick on this desk prints the desk that priced it and none is described as market consensus.

flags.title: Race and stroke-play events are modelled as two-sided matches
flags.detail: Greyhound races, motor races and stroke-play golf are multi-runner events. Several inherited rows invent a second side called 'Field', 'Remaining Belfast Field' or 'Inside Seeding Traps 1-3' and then quote a two-way price against it. That is not a market OLBG or any governing body publishes. This desk keeps those rows visible but labels them multi-runner and does not publish a match-winner pick from them.

flags.title: One scoreline is credited to two different players on adjacent rows
flags.detail: Row TN01 says Tsitsipas beat Karen Khachanov 4-6 7-6(5) 7-6(5); row TN02 says Bublik beat Karen Khachanov in a 4-6 7-6(5) 7-6(5) thriller lasting 32 games, in the same semi-final round of the same tournament. Khachanov cannot have lost that identical scoreline twice. Both rows are treated as unreliable for that detail and the detail is excluded from this desk's predictions for the two matches.
